units.translation: heaven
heaven
of what sort?
propping the pillar of heaven and earth on his shoulders
to one of those from heaven
to meet with the heaven gleaming with stars
sends to heaven – words
worshipping earth and heaven
the heaven blazing beneath the stars
for from heaven and from earth meadow dews were sprinkling down
and from the sea's dew and from heaven
Apollo, a god exiled from heaven
the holy heaven longs to wound the earth
and rain falling from the ever-flowing heaven
but my fate, reaching its fulfillment in heaven above
if I could have a cloak equal to heaven
of what sort?
heaven-supporting
heaven-supporting
the children of Atlas – they were weeping for their father's greatest labor, the heaven-supporting one
holding the heavens
holding the heavens
to revere the heaven-holding power
to speed with a fair wind
to speed with a fair wind
to speed the same fortune of fate always with a fair wind
by saying or doing what could I succeed in speeding you with a fair wind?
fair, favorable
fair, favorable
of a favoring god
The epithet οὔριος [fair, favorable] is frequent in places, on which see Thes. vol. 5 p. 2411.
wishing a favorable outcome
Zeus of fair winds
fair, favorable
prosperously established
prosperously established
we shall establish a female law that is prosperously established
fair wind
fair wind
let it go with a fair wind
of lamentations, dear friends, row with a fair wind the escorting stroke of your hands about your head
with a fair wind they raise a flight that is not orderly
ear
ear
of an eye observing something
Hence the eyes of the Persian king are spoken of, on which see Pollux 2, 84
in this sense
Improperly the moon is called the eye of night, the light of night.
about Tiresias
Thus Elmsley for ἀχάεσσα τούς [the unceasing ... these].
Thus Schuetz corrected what is in M διαμπερισῶς [through and through], changed by the same hand to διαμπερές ὡς [through and through as].
of Xerxes, where Stanley collected passages from other writers.
About Orestes, who is like a light to the family,
Of the same kind is what Atossa says

where nothing is noted in the old scholia, but the Byzantine scholiast explains ἤγουν ἀμφὶ τῷ Ξέρξῃ · ὀφθαλμὸν γὰρ ἐκεῖνον καλεῖ [that is, around Xerxes; for he calls him an eye], rightly, as it seems, although he did not notice what Hermann warned against him, that ὀφθαλμόν [eye] is said in the singular number of that which is dear to someone, unless where there is talk of several, as in the passage of Plautus mentioned in Thes. vol. 5 p. 2450, where those are the ones to whom you are eyes. From which it follows that in Aeschylus ὀφθαλμῷ [with an eye] should be written with Heimsoeth (Krit. Stud. 1 p. 72).
distributing in ears and mind
the destructive lament sends a great cry of the house to the ear
and a shout cries in the ears
passing through the ears and the mind of the people
this came through and through to the ear like a missile
listen, holding it in your ear
I shall have a faithful day-watching eye
and some were called ears and eyes of the king, those who reported what was said and done
your own faithful eye of the Persians, all of him
and the bright full moon in the middle of the shield, the eldest star, the eye of night, is conspicuous
that the eye of the house may not fall in utter destruction
and fear is in their eyes, for I consider the presence of the master the eye of the house
the unceasing ... these
